svg.text: FIGURE 5
STEP 8 · THE REAL PART AND THE FINITE FORM
RH: THE REAL PART AND ONE BIT · MASTER v3.0.39_CC · EVERY NAME CHECKED
STEP 8 · THE REAL PART, UNCONDITIONAL AT EVERY COMPUTED HEIGHT, AND THE FINITE FORM
THE SCHEMA, ON NO AXIOM
A certificate at T, a complete list of the zeros up to T with a
check that each lies on the line, yields the real part at T, for
every zero set with natural heights. No computation is an
input: each certificate is the hypothesis of its own instance.

svg.text: AT ζ, CITED AT THEIR OWN GRADE
Interval checks are true bounded sentences, theorems of PA
and ZFC; the evaluation bound of Hardy's function, Turing's
method as Lehman corrected it, and the Riemann–von
Mangoldt count; no real zero. Conjugation is proved in the
master.

tspan.font-family: RHMono, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

svg.text: THE HEIGHT AT ζ
The height of a zero is ⌈|Im s|⌉, a function of the Im s that
registration keeps; RH is the real part at every height.

svg.text: UNCONDITIONAL AT EVERY COMPUTED HEIGHT
At every height any computation certifies, now or in the
future, every nontrivial zero with |Im s| ≤ T lies on the line: a
theorem of ZFC.

svg.text: binds the chain, nothing before the colon
BELOW EVERY CERTIFIED HEIGHT THE BIT IS RECORDED; ABOVE IT, NONE IS
PHYSICO-FORMAL
Every finite computation to height T is a verified world below T: registering its
certified zeros is lossless and costs nothing at any positive temperature, and the
compute loop holds the record's idempotence and the cargo's least erasure with
no premise.

svg.text: WHAT THE KERNEL DOES NOT DO
It re-checks no certificate's numerics and constructs no certificate at any height:
a certificate at T is a computation on ζ, carrying the grade of whoever certifies it.
Read at every height, the family is the bit.
